q: Product reveal where it slowly emerges from total darkness.
a: Lumetri on the clip (`effects.apply`, `lumetri`) with Exposure keyframed from very low to normal over two or three seconds, eased (`effects.setInterpolation`); or a black Color Matte above with its Opacity keyframed from 100 % to 0. A soft light sweep (an ellipse mask on the matte, Inverted, moving across) makes it feel lit rather than faded.

q: light sweeps across the product revealing it
a: A black Color Matte on top with a feathered rectangle mask (Inverted) whose position is keyframed across the product, so the 'light' passes over it; a Wonder Glow on the product's highlights during the pass adds shine.

q: Reveal the scene from black with the sound swelling up.
a: Fade from black (a Dip to Black at the start, or Opacity keyed up) and keyframe the music / ambience Volume up over the same seconds (or an Exponential Fade transition from silence).

q: Glossy car commercial look for my friend's car.
a: Balance first, then a look node: deep blacks and strong contrast (S-curve), cool shadows and slightly warm highlights, Saturation restrained; a qualifier on the paint colour to make it rich. Speed and energy from the edit: short shots, a few slow-motion pieces (Speed / Duration, Optical Flow), a Lens Flare on a highlight.

q: reflections on the car paint look dull
a: Lift the highlights on the paint with a qualifier or a window on its own node (Gain up, a little contrast), keeping the rest; Glint or Wonder Glow on the brightest reflections for sparkle. Don't clip them: check the waveform.

q: Car driving at night: make the headlights and city lights pop.
a: Deep blacks, a cool grade, the lights pushed with qualifiers (keep them from clipping flat with soft clip), Wonder Glow with a high Threshold for bloom; noise reduction first on high-ISO night footage.

q: Turn a weekend of festival footage into a 2-minute aftermovie.
a: 1. Selects: the best crowd, stage and friends moments (markers, subclips, a bin per day). 2. A strong track fitted to two minutes with Remix (`clip.remix.enable`); cut to its phrases, faster in the drops. 3. Slow-motion crowd shots and flares for the emotional parts, Glitch or Light Leak transitions sparingly. 4. One warm, punchy grade copied across; loudness about −14 LUFS for online.

q: aftermovie: mix of phone and camera footage, different colours
a: Set each source's input colour space, match the phones to the camera (less sharpening, softer contrast, skin matched), then copy one look node to all (`grade.append`).

q: Crowd noise and music from the stage are a mess in my clips.
a: Use the song as the main audio and keep camera sound only for a few moments (cheers), typed Ambience and low, with short crossfades; Ducking the song under any speaking moments.

q: Start close on one photo and zoom out to show it's part of a wall of photos.
a: Build the wall in a comp: a Media In per photo, each through a Transform node (scale and position on a grid), merged together; a Transform after the merge whose Scale is keyframed from the one photo filling the frame down to the whole wall, eased. Many photos: nest groups to keep the graph readable.

q: grid of 9 videos that zooms into the middle one
a: Nine clips on tracks or in a comp, each scaled to a third and placed on the grid; nest them (`clip.nest`) and keyframe the nest's Scale and Position into the centre tile, then cut to that clip full-frame.

q: Wall zoom gets soft at the start because the photo is small.
a: The first photo needs enough resolution to fill the frame when zoomed in: use a large original for that one, or start the zoom less close.

q: A person stands frozen while the world keeps moving around them.
a: Locked-off camera. The live shot on V1 (people moving); on V2 a Frame Hold of the person (`clip.frameHold`) at a moment they're still, with a feathered mask around them on Opacity (`masks.add`) so only the frozen person sits over the moving world. Moving people must not cross in front of them, or they'll vanish behind the hold.

q: time-lapse world behind a person standing still
a: Shoot long on a tripod. Background: the clip sped up (Speed / Duration, e.g. 1000 %); foreground: the person from a normal-speed moment (or a Frame Hold) masked on top. They must hold still enough for the mask to work.

q: My frozen person's edge shows the moving background through it.
a: Tighten and feather the mask more carefully (Mask Expansion, Feather), and keyframe it if the person sways; plain backgrounds behind the edge help.

q: Punchy zoom burst on a hit, like in action edits.
a: On the hit frame: a fast Scale push of 3–5 frames (Transform effect with Use Effect Shutter Angle for motion blur), Camera Shake for a few frames after, and a Zoom Blur or Cross Zoom transition if it lands on a cut. A hit sound on the same frame.

q: zoom punch on every beat drop
a: Make one burst, save it as a preset (`presets.save`, keyframes anchored to the In point), cut at each drop and apply it to the clip after the cut.

q: Speed-ramp into the punch for extra impact.
a: A stepped ramp: the build-up faster, the hit at normal speed or slow (Add Edit + Speed / Duration per piece), then the zoom burst and shake on the hit frame.

q: Stock clips I bought look too clean next to my own footage.
a: Match them to your footage: balance and contrast to your look (Shot Match against a still of your shot, then refine), lower saturation if stock is punchier, add grain to the stock clips to match texture, and the same look node on both.

q: stock is 24fps but my project is 25fps
a: Conform it: set its speed so it plays at 25 (about 104 %, frame sampling) for no stutter, or leave it at 100 % and accept a repeated frame each second; for slow-motion stock shot at high frame rates, set the speed so every frame shows.

q: Stock footage in Rec.709 and my F-Log2 in one look.
a: Set the stock's input colour space to Rec. 709 and your clips to F-Log2 so both land in the working space; grade the hero (your footage) first and match the stock to it.

q: The cheesy 'zoom and enhance' effect on security footage.
a: Steps of punch-in: cut the clip into a few pieces, each scaled further (Motion Scale) on the detail, a Mosaic (pixelation) that gets finer each step and finally off, a little Sharpen, and a beep on each step. A rectangle shape outlining the area before each zoom sells the 'computer'.

q: enhance effect with scanning lines and a timecode
a: Add the VHS shader or a scanline overlay on the zoomed pieces and a Metadata & Timecode Burn-in for the security-cam timecode; text graphics for 'ENHANCING…'.

q: The zoomed-in frame looks too blurry even for the joke.
a: Zooming past the footage's resolution softens it: start from higher-resolution footage, or embrace it with stronger pixelation steps; Sharpen only a little (halos).

q: Flash a single frame of a scary image for a split second.
a: Cut a one-frame (or two-frame) piece of the image into the sequence at the moment (place it and trim to one frame with the trim keys); a sound hit on the same frame. Note: flashing images can trouble some viewers, so use sparingly.

q: several quick flash frames building tension
a: Several 1–3 frame inserts, closer together towards the climax, with hits on each; markers make placing them on the music easy.

q: Flash frame that's also distorted and red.
a: On the inserted frame: a red push in Lumetri or the node grader and a Glitch shader or Turbulent Displace for distortion; GPU-only shader effects need a working graphics card.

q: Text like 'Tokyo — 3:00 AM' appearing at the start of a scene.
a: A text graphic in a clean font, lower left inside the safe margins, fading in with eased Opacity keyframes and out after a few seconds; save it as a template with the text editable for every location.

q: location card that types itself letter by letter
a: Reveal it with a rectangle mask on the text graphic whose edge is keyframed left to right in steps (Hold keyframes), plus a typing sound; per-character styles keyed by hand also work.

q: Same location card style throughout a documentary.
a: One template (`graphics.template.export`) with the place and time editable, applied at each scene (`graphics.template.apply`); keep one typeface and size system across the film.
